text:
Evgeni Malkin is 40, a pending free agent, and the most talked-about trade chip in the league this week. The Minnesota Wild keep coming up in the rumors (Bolavip and others reported Minnesota's interest after it failed to land Dylan Larkin), and the questions are all the same: would Pittsburgh move him, and would he go?

What makes it a real conversation is that he can still play. Malkin has 20 points in 20 games, eight of them on the power play, and he came back from his latest absence with two power-play points against Calgary. That night also moved him past Bryan Trottier into 19th on the NHL's all-time points list.

His game has narrowed to what he does best. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 96th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season, and 11 of his last 13 points are assists. The cost is the other end: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on the ice than with almost any other forward. A contender would be buying the passing and covering for the rest.
